QCut-owned manual body stretch: a manual-body stage (after skin, before face shaping, as in the native order) renders the editor's stretch band with geometry measured from the native tool on coordinate-encoded frames; the canonical plan carries manualBody only when a tool changes the picture, so existing plans and receipts are unchanged; plan validation, resident contract and original-resolution support extended to it.

QCut-owned manual body slim and zoom: the manual-body stage also renders the editor's slim rectangle (a displacement table measured from the native tool on coordinate-encoded frames, one shape for every size and orientation, linear in intensity) and zoom circle (a fitted radial profile), applied after the stretch in the native order; plan validation and the planner accept their editor ranges and keep only tools that change the picture, so existing plans and receipts are unchanged.

QCut-owned smart long leg (body_adjust_StretchLeg): a smart-body stage after makeup, as in the native order. The still-frame pose follows the effect's own path, measured on real render tensors: the frame scaled to a 640 long side, the coarse fixed-point body network seeding two 192x144 refinement passes (NumPy interpreter, bit-exact with the native CPU networks; weights from the private runtime asset body-skeleton-v1.npz). The leg descriptor, state, 30x30 mesh and Metal draw port the 2026-10-17 independent research chain; the still-frame descriptor update count is fitted to native renders. Body controls are named body_adjust_* and map only to catalog controls of the body group; existing plans are unchanged.

QCut-owned smart body, all ten sliders (small head, swan neck, slim arms, square shoulders, shoulder width, slim body, slim waist, long legs, bust, hip shape) in one smart-body stage after makeup. The per-joint status, head, public measurements, torso basis, ten part descriptors and states, and the composed 30x30 mesh port the 2026-10-17 independent research chain verbatim in float32 order (byte-identical to it on 138 cold, persistent and randomized cases; its accepted mesh matched the effect bit for bit). Faces come from the engine's own detector and alignment networks; Stage1 can recompute yaw and pitch in the effect's four-lane fused order (pose_heads, off unless asked). A still frame is the component after eight updates of the still pose, where the effect's photo renders were measured to settle. The long-leg-only state, mesh and renderer are replaced.

A still image is searched for a face once when the search finds no single usable face: the image and the detector do not change across the eight updates, so the repeats only added latency. The body still takes all eight updates.

Owned body temporal research: explicit persistent single-person mode2 session, native missing-leg tracker crop, video classification and same-frame redetection lifecycle, bounded replay/cancellation contract, optional exact ONNX integer interpreter, and native-rule finite manual zoom mesh. Numeric CPU probes and original renderer comparisons are private evidence; source contains no vendor binaries, shaders, weights, model policy tables, or recorded landmarks. The production photo runner retains its accepted eight same-image updates; the cold body_smart_candidate and namespaced temporal modules remain explicit research APIs; the optional video policy is required only by the explicit sequence API. Manual zoom uses only owned numeric code and public Metal.

Restore the pinned native five-slot video face lifecycle: independent slot histories, retained-face matching, cold detector-index allocation and recovery first-free allocation, monotonic IDs, native detection cadence, delayed publication of 160-only seeds, current-ID output order, and ordered FilterDup suppression. Optional exact classification terminals preserve native float32 FMA and scalar softmax order for video gates and duplicate confidence without changing default photo heads. Checkpoint v2 captures all five slot histories without model handles and reattaches shared models on restore. Regression coverage includes active recovery, slot loss and reentry, duplicate boundaries, classifier terminals, and checkpoint continuation. The body renderer remains a single-body profile; private model weights, original libraries, probe captures, and runtime assets remain private and unchanged.

Restore native missing-body per-frame advancement: preserve skeleton history while descriptor intensities and deformation caches continue, render retained residual geometry, and apply native face selection when the body or face result is empty. Add the pinned video component input type 0, fixed 60-column/75-row mesh, hard-reset descriptor sentinels, native reliability weighting, long-leg state inputs, and per-vertex SmallHead/SlimHip/SlimArm temporal accumulation. Use native float texture sampling with unflipped source pixels and fragment UV-Y inversion. Preserve native control-value and explicit reapply events, including pending vertex-history invalidation across inactive frames and checkpoints. Cover absent-body cancellation, render failure, decay/reentry, and checkpoint continuation with both persistent and native video profiles. Stateless photo profile and manual-body scope remain separate. Private models, binaries, native captures, and runtime asset rows remain unchanged.

Restore native timestamp-driven component input types: first-frame mode 1, mode 0 above a 0.01-second interval, and mode 2 at or below that interval, including native per-vertex history reset gates. Reject intervals above 0.1 seconds before advancing state and require replay. Bump body-session snapshot schema to v3 because the former mode-2 geometry profile and its cached mesh cannot resume in the native 60-column/75-row video profile; refuse v2 snapshots before any session restart, loaded-model change, history mutation, or clock change. Add an independent compatibility regression and refresh timestamp-boundary tests. Preserve all prior import provenance and all private runtime asset rows unchanged.

Restore the video profile with absolute timestamp-driven component input modes and exact warm IMAGE resets, preserving perception, strengths, retained-but-uninitialized vertex filter storage and shoulder counters according to native virtual-reset fields rather than rebuilding the session. Add Python-only ordered RESET_PARAMS/set_control events, with complete validation before mutation, native clock reset and same-value reapply semantics; submission frame order remains independent of repeated, reversed or jumping finite nonnegative timestamps. Snapshot v4 captures the native effect clock and filter initialized state and rejects older incompatible schemas before session mutation. Cover control order, absence/reentry, warm-reset field retention, cancellation/render failure, and exact checkpoint replay. Existing worker/Electron event transport and cache contracts remain closed to these Python-only events. Stateless photo and manual-body scope remain separate. Private models, binaries, captures, imported sourceSha256 provenance, and all runtime asset rows remain unchanged.
